subject: axolotl
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.

spec.name: Chibi Axolotl
spec.description: A chibi axolotl with a huge round head, tiny stubby body and legs, a finned tail and three big frilly pink gills on each side.
spec.layout: Chibi proportions: a giant wide flat-topped head at the front (+Z) about 55% of the body length, a short chubby body behind it, four stubby legs with tiny splayed toes resting on the floor, and a thick tail curving gently behind with a continuous low dorsal fin running from the head down the back to the tail tip. Each side of the head has three feathery gills fanning out sideways and upward, built as stalks with many small pink fronds in a root-to-tip palette from deep rose to pale pink. Face: two big glossy black eyes with white highlights on top-front of the head, a wide smiling mouth line, tiny nostril dots, and rosy blush cheeks. Pale pink-peach body with a lighter belly. Everything is blocky low-poly primitives with flat colours.

parts.builds: The big flat-topped rounded head: wide skull loft in skin colour, pale chin/belly underside, upper and lower jaw as separate pieces on jaw joint with a dark mouth line and tiny tongue, two large glossy black eyes with white highlights and tiny rim, nostril dots, blush cheek discs, a few darker spots on top, small brow bumps.
parts.attaches: Meets the body at neckJoin; gill roots at gillRootL/R sit on its sides; the dorsal fin begins at finStart on its top.

parts.builds: Six feathery gill assemblies (3 per side): each a thin curved stalk in gillStalk with 6-9 small flat frond blades/spikes along it, graded gillStalk to gillMid to gillTip, fanning outward and upward from the head sides in a tiered fan, bigger on top, slightly longer outward. Each stalk has a small rounded base nub seated on the head.
parts.attaches: Roots at gillRootL and gillRootR on the head sides, riding the gillL1-3 and gillR1-3 joints.

parts.builds: The chubby short torso loft in skin colour with a pale belly sector underneath, spots along the back, a low rounded back ridge, and the continuous dorsal fin start from finStart along the back to tailBase as a thin extruded scalloped fin in fin colour with small rib lines.
parts.attaches: Front joins the head at neckJoin, rear joins the tail at tailBase, legs at shoulderL/R and hipL/R.

parts.builds: Four stubby chubby legs, each a short two-segment tube splayed outward and forward/back, ending in a flat round foot pad with four tiny rounded toes in toe colour, resting on the floor; slightly darker skin on the outer sides.
parts.attaches: Roots at shoulderL/R and hipL/R on the body sides.

parts.builds: A thick tail tapering and flattening vertically (paddle shaped) with a gentle S curve, skin colour with pale underside, topped by a tall tapered fin along its top edge and a smaller fin underneath, rounded tip, spots and fin ribs in darker pink.
parts.attaches: Starts at tailBase where the body ends; continues the dorsal fin line from the body.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out the leg joint structure, building tube segments from shoulder to elbow and then down to the foot so each leg reaches the floor properly.

Still placing feet and toes...

Clock-based sectors feel too fiddly for a leg tube oriented sideways-and-down, so I'm dropping that approach and instead placing small darker surface spots directly on the outer side of the upper leg for shading.

Working out how to add darker skin spots and an elbow knob along the legs, plus thinking through a wrist cuff band — trying a ring of points around a frame but wrestling with getting the correct orientation since sweep gives normal-facing frames rather than tangent ones.

Now I'm working out the leg geometry — front leg from shoulder through elbow to wrist to foot, checking lengths stay within the body box, then mirroring the approach for the hind leg with knee and foot placement and toe extension toward the back.

Adding more joint details...

Placing spots along the upper leg sweep at several t-values with rays cast outward to find surface positions, then adding a wrist band near the end of the sweep.

I'm planning the gill joints for the head, setting positions and directions for three joints on each side symmetrically.

Now I'm working out the actual frond shapes — fanning each tier outward and upward, with the top gills larger, and sketching bezier-like stalk paths that taper across the bounding box before attaching flat blade fronds along each stalk's sweep.

Defining the leaf outline shape...

For orientation, I need the blade's extrude plane to have perpendicular axes: frond direction d tilts from the stalk tangent T by some angle, so I'll derive y as the component of T orthogonal to d, normalized, giving thickness along their cross product.

Now I'm working out per-station geometry: computing up and forward vectors orthogonal to the tangent at each point, then setting fronds at roughly 55° angles alternating between up/down and front/back directions to avoid generating too many parts across stations and gills.

Defining stalk and frond geometry per tier...

I'm adjusting tier3's stalk to dip down slightly with shorter fronds to stay within the box, and nudging the z-depth fan so tiers 1-3 sweep back progressively for a natural gill curve. Now I'm starting to lay out the actual path points.

I'm defining the tier positions and tip coordinates, then building a gentle upward-curving path through control points using Catmull-Rom interpolation so the gill curls slightly at the end.

Now I'm setting up bone-based rigid binding for the sweep so each joint controls its segment properly, then spacing out frond stations along the stalk from base to tip with varying blade lengths scaled by position.

Still tuning frond geometry...

I'm also working out the angle progression and perpendicular direction alternation for each frond, and assigning gradient colors along the stalk so fronds shift in hue from base to tip.

Thinking about adding a tiny bulb at each stalk's tip for visual detail, and tallying up total part counts per gill to decide whether to adjust the number of stations.

I also work out the geometry for extrusion: computing a perpendicular direction vector from the tangent, deriving orthogonal axes for thickness, and defining the extrude parameters (position, orientation, thickness, color, bone) needed for the mesh outline.

Now I'm structuring the gill joints by iterating over left/right sides and tier levels, naming them systematically like gillL1, gillR2, etc., and adding small stalk nubs attached to each joint with slight scaling adjustments for visual variety.

I'm planning the buildBody function, defining a bounding box for the torso and lofting stations along the z-axis from the hips up to the chest to shape the body form.

I'm also figuring out a tail fin that rises from the body top around the head area, and deciding whether to use a sweep with a radius function tied to the hips-chest bone so I can apply belly color sectors, running the path from rear to front along the center line.

Calculating vertical radius ranges so the body stays within the bounding box, then checking the end caps—round caps would extend the shape past the box edges, so I'll need flat caps or a shortened path to keep the tail and head within bounds.

Now I'm setting the body proportions with the center and radii, placing a belly color sector underneath and deciding to skip a dorsal stripe in favor of scattered spots for texture. I'm adding small flattened spot shapes across the upper surface using a scatter pattern filtered by surface normal direction.

I'm also thinking through a subtle raised ridge along the back, sweeping a slightly darker tube shape from hips to chest, though I need to work out how bones attach to a swept path that isn't tied to the main skeleton.

For the fin, I'm now defining its outline in the z-y plane, positioning its base embedded into the body's top surface near the front, and shaping a scalloped profile that rises and dips in crests toward the back.

Still shaping scallop geometry...

I'm tapering the fin height from front to back, keeping the tail end roughly matched to the body envelope there. For the mesh itself, I'm giving it a slight thickness with a small bevel, coloring it as the fin material, and planning to rig it across the chest/hip bones using separate extrusions per bone segment.

Splitting the fin into front (chest) and rear (hips) segments, I'm writing a shared outline function so the scallop pattern stays continuous across the boundary -- aligning the segment edges at a scallop valley so the seam looks seamless.

Adding a smooth ramp at the front tip and a taper at the rear so the fin height eases in and out rather than cutting off abruptly, then adding thin rib lines up the fin face for texture.

Writing rib and bone placement code...

I'm thinking about adding tiny decorative touches — small cute nubs at each fin peak, maybe a gradient rim on the fin edge, and considering subtle belly details like a navel line or soft pads near the hip and shoulder bumps.

I'm placing skin-toned blobs at the shoulder and hip joints where the legs attach, sized to sit naturally against the body's curve, and I'm thinking about scattering small flank spots along the sides and back for that speckled axolotl look.

Adding dorsal spot scatter...

I'm also considering a subtle ridge line running along the back beneath the fin in the darker skin tone, tapered thin so it peeks out on either side as a natural seam.

Now I'm sketching the outline function, defining an envelope curve that tapers along body length with a sinusoidal top profile for silhouette variation.

Ribs placed at regular intervals along the fin, skipping the gap region, running from just above the base to just below the peak. No new joints needed, just reusing the existing body part prefix, so this is ready to finalize.

I'm setting up a buildHead function that takes the joints object with neck, head, and jaw, planning the head box dimensions symmetric around the center axis.

I'm placing the head joint near the front for aiming and the jaw joint at the front tip as a hinge point, then sketching the skull as a scaled sphere primitive and considering a loft for a flatter top shape, with the lower jaw sitting beneath as a separate rigid piece.

Defining loft stations...

For the underside, I'm planning a pale scaled sphere positioned to hug the belly beneath the chin, and starting to think about adding the lower jaw as a separate piece.

Now I'm working out the jaw as a pale-pink scaled sphere, then figuring out how to draw the mouth as a thin dark curved sweep across the front using points that follow the skull's curvature, considering whether to use a ray-casting approach to seat the mouth line against the skull surface.

Adjusting jaw front position slightly and giving it a pale belly tone. I'll tuck a small pale-red tongue sphere near the front of the jaw, mostly hidden since the mouth stays closed, skipping any jaw-opening pose since rotating around the front tip looks awkward.

Now I'm placing the eyes near the top-front of the skull, using a downward raycast from above to find the surface at each x/z position and embedding small flattened black spheres there.

Still computing eye placement...

Now I'm figuring out the blush marks as small flat discs on the cheeks, positioning them at an angle avoiding the gill attachment points, with rays cast outward from the front-lower cheek area to find the surface normal for embedding.

I'm also adding brow bumps as small flattened skin-colored spheres above the eyes, a darker rim sphere behind each eye for depth, and scattering small flattened spot cylinders across the top of the head using downward rays at several x,z positions.

Then I'm considering whether to add a cranium crest ridge or snout bridge detail but deciding to skip both, and planning a neck collar sphere at the head-body junction to smoothly connect the head to the body mesh.

Next I'm thinking about small finishing touches—darker dimple dots at the mouth corners, a pale chin patch—and sketching out the bone hierarchy with separate head, jaw, and tongue parts before setting up a surface helper to compute ray intersections against the skull.

For hitting features like nostrils and the smile line, I'm reasoning through how to cast rays toward the face, accounting for curvature so the sampled points sit correctly at the mouth corners where the surface slopes inward.

I'm plotting the mouth curve as a sequence of points from the side ray-hits inward to the front, checking that the catmull interpolation between a side point and a front point doesn't dip through the face surface near the cheek transition.

Switching to elevation-based offsets instead works better since it keeps points on the surface, using a small angle that scales with azimuth squared to curve the mouth naturally. I'm bounding the azimuth range to around ±70° so the mouth ends near the gill root rather than overshooting into the side.

Now I'm positioning the blush just above and behind where the mouth ends, using surface normal placement at a specific azimuth/elevation so it sits correctly on the cheek. I still need to figure out the lower jaw -- considering making it a separate scaled sphere piece, but need to check it doesn't poke below the skull's existing geometry.

Splitting the skull into two lofts: an upper skull loft centered higher up with a smaller bottom extent, and a separate lower jaw loft positioned below it, joining at a seam near the mouth line around y 0.105. I'm working out station widths and heights across the jaw's z-range so it tapers correctly and meets the skull cleanly at the lip.

I'm setting the jaw as a single-joint loft with a pale belly-like underside near the chin, keeping the skull color on top, and adding a tiny tongue tucked near the mouth seam that's likely hidden between the overlapping surfaces.

Moving on to finalizing the part count around 50, I'm planning to write the actual loft code with jaw bone and color options, deciding to pass a sides parameter for smoother sweeps, and setting up raycasts to position eyes on the skull surface.

Working out eye geometry now: placing flattened spheres for rim, dark iris, and small highlight spheres offset along the surface normal so the eyes sit naturally on the curved skull.

Now I'm positioning small brow-bump ellipsoids just behind the eye sockets, using a scaled sphere geometry helper to get the flattened shape right.

Then I'm setting up the palette keys for skin, belly, eyes, mouth, blush, and spots, and sketching how the cheek blush will layer a larger soft disc with a brighter inner disc on top, guarding against null hit results when placing them on the surface.

Adding mouth corner dimples with tiny dark spheres and a neck collar ellipsoid sized to fit within the body bounds...

I'm planning to build the tail using a bone chain across joints tail1 through tail4, lofting a tapered box shape along their positions to form the tail geometry.

Switching to a sweep approach instead, with a path curving slightly in x and y through the joint positions, and varying radii so the tail tapers from thick at the base to thin at the tip while accommodating the fin shape's vertical extent.

Now I'm working on the fins, extruding outlines in the z,y plane for the dorsal fin, basing it along the tail's top edge but sinking the fin base slightly into the tube for a natural join.

Still plotting fin outline coordinates... I realize the fin spans multiple tail bones, so rigid extrusion won't bend properly — I need to split the fin into separate pieces per joint, each rigged to its own bone, and plan a helper function to generate each segment's outline between two u-values.

Still working out fin geometry...

Working out sampling for the dorsal fin scallop pattern, using a triangle wave with aligned boundaries, and checking the tail fin extends to match where the tail tube ends near z -0.9.

I'm setting the envelope points tapering the fin width down to 0.035 at the tip, confirming the top stays above the base edge throughout. Then I'm working out the fin's thickness profile, tapering from 0.012 at the base to 0.004 near the top, and computing the cross product to get the perpendicular direction for extruding that thickness.

Now I'm adding a smaller ventral fin beneath the body, spanning from u=0.2 to 0.6 with its own height envelope peaking around 0.055 at u=0.4, and working out how far below the tube's bottom edge it should sit.

Tweaking the tail's radius shrink curve for the paddle taper, then sketching a gentle S-curve path for the body's y and x coordinates so the fins can follow that same sway.

I work out that using the segment's slope as the shear vector gives a thickness axis that stays roughly aligned with x, with only negligible length distortion from the sway. Now I need to figure out the actual path functions, mapping the catmull-rom parameter to get xc and yc at any point along the curve.

Since the tail joint sits slightly into the path, I'll start the tube a bit before z=-0.3 so it's hidden inside the body, using a flat cap at the start and round at the end. Then I'm mapping radius along the total path length for the fin segments.

Now I'm adding small darker spot markings along the tail using flattened cylinders placed at various points along the tube, oriented using sweep frames, with angles varying on both sides to scatter roughly ten spots of different sizes.

I'm also sketching thin rib rods across the fin faces, running from base to near the top at several positions, using narrow four-sided rods offset slightly from center to give subtle surface detail while following the fin's tapering thickness.

Mapping out rib placement along u, with roughly 28 dorsal ribs and 16 ventral ones, bound to nearby joints, then adding a belly color sector and deciding fin and rib tints using the pink/spot palette.

Now I'm working out the fin segment boundaries and making sure the extrusion polygons avoid self-intersection, tracking top and base points relative to the bone's shifting center. I'm drafting a helper function to build each fin segment given its endpoints, shape functions, bone reference, color, and thickness.

Orientation shouldn't matter either way. For the ventral fin, I'm mapping segments across u=0.18 to 0.6, checking that the envelope and tube radius taper together so the fin tip stays thin and stays within the tube's end cap near u≈0.615.

Now I'm working out the scallop pattern along the dorsal fin using a triangle wave for ridges, then setting up a lookup helper for interpolation and planning how to place cylindrical spot details along the tube's sweep path at varying angles and sizes.

Still writing sweep code...

Still writing rib placement logic...
